title: Vibed this in a few hours with GPT 5.6 sol and GoDot Engine
author: clean_rebel29
selftext:
Free Unity Store assets for the environment.  
Mixamo characters for the animations.  
GoDot Engine

Top-down ARPG perspective that lets the user shift to 3rd person behind the shoulder classic RPG style perspective. 

Honestly, I'm thoroughly impressed at how much can be done with these tools.

comments.author: Opposite_Age_1414
comments.body:
The problems come down the line after couple of months of work when a lot of game systems have to work together. That is why real devs with much experience will be much more effective with AI then just vibe coders. That doesen't mean you shouldn't try and have fun or maybe that you even make something great. But understanding what is under the hood would help you a lot. 

On other side players don't give damn for what is under hood, they care that is working and that is fun, no bugs. So good luck!

replies.author: SurvivalHermit
replies.body:
Agentic tools aren't only going to get you half way. You can contrary to popular opinion learn about engineering while vibe coding. You make it sound like building things the exact wrong way isn't a problem every first time developer faces. Like people who have a CS degree magically made all the right decisions the first time they made a game and didn't spend literal years building a bridge with no supports that crumbled 2 years in. The difference is with AI tools you are going to see the fractures much faster because its getting built faster. 

Using AI to code and create software is a skill just like any other. There is significant overlap with the knowledge and understanding that traditional coders have but not all coding knowledge is useful for AI coding and traditional coding does not include 100% of the knowledge needed to succeed with AI. Its almost like Its a new tool with a whole new set of fundamentals that happens to overlap with the old way of doing things.

Saying vibe coding will only get you so far is just wrong. its like a painter telling a photographer that their pictures will never be as good if they don't first learn to paint. Is there a lot of overlap sure but you can do one without the other.

replies.author: Opposite_Age_1414
replies.body: Yes, and all coders I know use AI for coding that is not the point. Architectural design and systems that will clash with each other months later are. That doesn't mean vibe coding is bad or vibe coding can't make a good game becaue player don't care about spagetti code if game is fun, everything work and no bugs. I am making my game game vibe coding, apart of code I do everything myself. My friend who is C++ professor provides me guiding for structure and architecture. And still in months I made so many changes and mistakes, had to redo whole systems because I didn't know what with clash later on and had to make decisions without previous knowledge. And AI is not all knowing, and its pretty shortsighted and makes many simple and logical mistakes that we as humans catch easily if we know the matter well.

replies.author: mbrodie
replies.body:
This is incorrect you just need an understanding of the architectural layer and what actually goes into solid NetCode etc… 

It’s not impossible it’s just about how much time you’re willing to dedicate and how much you’re willing to learn as you go to know what to look out for.

There is a reason more and more game studios are starting to use LLMs along side their development processes….

There has already been multiple projects released that are fully functional “mmo” type games with hundreds to thousands of concurrent users etc…

You make it seem like there isn’t years of emulators and free game server examples around for the LLM to learn from.

It just comes down to a fundamental willingness to learn what goes into it and how everything builds together.
